# 16.Testing — State Map

> **What this file is:** Phase and task tracker for all work within `16.Testing`.
> **What it is not:** The root tracker — that lives at `state-map.md`.
> **Sync policy:** When all tasks under a Phase Key are `●`, run `/state-map-phase` with `phase_key: SK.16.{Phase}` to propagate that milestone to the root state-map.

---

## Legend

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `○` | Not started |
| `◐` | In progress |
| `●` | Complete |
| `⚑` | Blocked |
| `—` | N/A / Skipped |

---

## Phase Key Registry

> Phase keys are the sync bridge between this sub-state-map and the root `state-map.md`.
> Each key maps a local milestone to a root-level phase. When a key's Promotion Condition is met, the root is updated via `/state-map-phase`.

| Phase Key | Maps to Root Phase | Promotion Condition |
|-----------|---------------------|----------------------|
| `SK.16.Design` | Design | All tasks in Phase: Design are `●` |
| `SK.16.Scaffold` | Scaffold | All tasks in Phase: Scaffold are `●` |
| `SK.16.Core` | Core | All tasks in Phase: Core are `●` |
| `SK.16.Tests` | Tests | All tasks in Phase: Tests are `●` |
| `SK.16.Docs` | Docs | All tasks in Phase: Docs are `●` |
| `SK.16.Published` | Published | All tasks in Phase: Published are `●` |

| D-117 | Design the DELIBERATE NON-COUPLING between `InMemorySearchIndex<TDocument>`, `InMemorySearchIndexProvisioner`, and `InMemorySearchProviderDescriptor` — unlike a real provider package (where all three interfaces, for the SAME provider, share one DI-root's internal state), the three `Search/` fakes are fully INDEPENDENT with no constructor or type dependency on each other. Rationale: `InMemorySearchIndex<TDocument>` is generic per document type and by far the most commonly needed fake (a consumer testing a query handler that depends on `ISearchIndex<TDocument>` alone); `ISearchIndexProvisioner`/`ISearchProviderDescriptor` are non-generic and needed only by a consumer specifically testing rebuild-orchestration or startup pre-flight-validation logic. Forcing all three to share one backing registry would add ceremony most `InMemorySearchIndex<TDocument>`-only tests never touch, and would not even achieve full real-provider fidelity, since `RegisteredIndexes`/`Validate`/`ProbeAsync.DocumentCount` are DEFINITION-derived on the real contract too, never live-`TDocument`-document-store-derived (except `DocumentCount`, which this fake fixes at `0` as a documented simplification, per D-115). > **DESIGN-PHASE DRIFT CORRECTION 2026-08-21** (testing-phase-implementer): D-204–D-208 were written against a `15.Integration/SharedKernel.Integration.Webhooks` snapshot that predates that domain's own WO-064 hardening pass (`SK.15.WO064`, P-421–P-429), which shipped 38/38 **after** these design rows were drafted and changed the exact target contract. Re-verified directly against the live `.cs` files (not `15.Integration/CLAUDE.md` prose, not the prior D-204–D-208 text) before writing any code:
> 1. **`IWebhookDispatcher` gained a third member** (P-429): `Task<WebhookDeliveryResult> SendTestDeliveryAsync(WebhookSubscription subscription, CancellationToken ct)`. D-204's original text covered only `DispatchAsync<TEvent>`/`DispatchToSubscriptionAsync<TEvent>` and does not compile against the real interface today.
> 2. **`WebhookDeliveryResult`'s positional constructor gained a second parameter** (P-423): now `(Guid SubscriptionId, Guid DeliveryId, bool IsSuccess, int? StatusCode, int Attempts, string? Error)` — six args, not five. D-204's originally-specified default (`new WebhookDeliveryResult(subscription.SubscriptionId, true, 200, 1, null)`) is a five-argument call against a six-parameter record and does not compile.
> 3. **`WebhookSubscription` also drifted** (re-checked, not assumed): `Secret` (single string) is now `Secrets` (`IReadOnlyList<string>`, newest-first, P-425) plus an obsolete back-compat `Secret` shim; and a new optional `Headers` property (`IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>?`, P-426) was added. Neither fake reads `Secrets`/`Headers` at all (both are pure recorder+configurable-result doubles that never construct or transform a `WebhookSubscription`, only echo the caller-supplied instance back through assertion helpers), so this drift has no code-shape consequence for either fake — recorded here as the explicit re-check the phase input required, not left as an unstated assumption.
>
> **Corrected design, superseding D-204's original text (D-205/D-206/D-207 needed no change — their target interfaces/behavior are unaffected by the WO-064 drift):** `InMemoryWebhookDispatcher` implements all three `IWebhookDispatcher` members, each with its own independent recording list and independent configurable-result mechanism (no internal delegation between members — a fake proves each interface member's own observable contract, not production's internal call-through):
> - `DispatchAsync<TEvent>` — records the raw event into `Dispatched` (`IReadOnlyList<object>`); configurable via `SetDispatchResult<TEvent>(Func<TEvent, IReadOnlyList<WebhookDeliveryResult>>)`; defaults to an empty list (unchanged from the original design).
> - `DispatchToSubscriptionAsync<TEvent>` — records `(SubscriptionId, event)` into `DispatchedTo`; configurable via `SetDispatchResult(Guid subscriptionId, WebhookDeliveryResult result)`; defaults to a synthetic 2xx success built with the CORRECTED six-arg constructor: `new WebhookDeliveryResult(subscription.SubscriptionId, Guid.NewGuid(), true, 200, 1, null)` — `DeliveryId` defaults to a fresh `Guid.NewGuid()` per call (an uninspected correlation identifier, not a business-assertable value; mirrors the established `EventEnvelopeBuilder`/`HttpClientHandlerTestFactory` precedent of using `Guid.NewGuid()` for correlation-shaped fields in this package, which this domain's own determinism rule already tolerates since no test asserts a specific `DeliveryId` value).
> - `SendTestDeliveryAsync` (NEW member, not in the original D-204 text) — records the `WebhookSubscription` into a new `TestDeliveries` list (`IReadOnlyList<WebhookSubscription>`), independent of `DispatchedTo`, since a ping delivery is observably distinct from a real event delivery; configurable via a new `SetTestDeliveryResult(Guid subscriptionId, WebhookDeliveryResult result)`, defaulting to the same synthetic-2xx shape. New assertion helper: `.ShouldHaveSentTestDelivery(Guid subscriptionId)` → void (throws if no matching test delivery was recorded), joining the four assertion helpers already specified in D-204 (`ShouldHaveDispatched<TEvent>()`/`ShouldNotHaveDispatched<TEvent>()`/`ShouldHaveDispatchedTo(Guid)` unchanged from the original design; `.Dispatched`/`.DispatchedTo` unchanged; `.TestDeliveries` newly added alongside them). Deliberately does NOT construct a real `WebhookPingEvent` and delegate through `DispatchToSubscriptionAsync` internally (unlike production's own documented "constructs a `WebhookPingEvent` and calls `DispatchToSubscriptionAsync<TEvent>` verbatim" behavior) — doing so would require either an unseeded `Guid.NewGuid()`/non-fixed `DateTimeOffset` inside the ping event's own construction (this fake's caller does not control that construction) or coupling the two members' result-configuration together, neither of which serves a fake whose only job is recording+configurable-result per member, not reproducing production's internal call graph.
> All corrected member signatures, the `WebhookDeliveryResult` six-arg construction, and the new `SendTestDeliveryAsync`/`TestDeliveries`/`SetTestDeliveryResult`/`ShouldHaveSentTestDelivery` surface are implemented verbatim in C-123 (`Integration/InMemoryWebhookDispatcher.cs`).
| D-209 | Design `FakeTenantCacheService` (sealed class, `Caching/`, implements the planned `ITenantCacheService` from `02.Caching/SharedKernel.Caching.Abstractions`, Phase 44/P-435/WO-065, `○` planned — sourced directly from `02.Caching/CLAUDE.md`'s ratified Interface Contracts + Implementation Rules prose, zero drift from the target shape, never guessed): backing store `ConcurrentDictionary<(string TenantId, string Entity, string Id), object?>` — the composite tuple key structurally guarantees two different `tenantId` values sharing the identical `(entity, id)` pair can never collide, satisfying this phase's own cross-tenant-isolation acceptance criterion BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a runtime check. `GetAsync<T>(tenantId, entity, id, ct)` → `ValueTask<T?>`; `SetAsync<T>(tenantId, entity, id, value, policy, ct)` → `ValueTask`; `GetOrSetAsync<T>(tenantId, entity, id, factory, policy, ct)` → `ValueTask<T>` (returns the cached value on a hit; on a miss, invokes `factory(ct)` exactly once, stores the result, then returns it); `RemoveAsync(tenantId, entity, id, ct)` → `ValueTask`; `RemoveByTagAsync(tenantId, tag, ct)` → `ValueTask`. Mirrors `02.Caching`'s own documented cross-tenant INVALIDATION-vector fix (its Implementation Rules state: "Tag tenant-scoping is mandatory... `TenantCacheService.SetAsync` rewrites every tag... to `{tenantId}:{tag}`... `RemoveByTagAsync` applies the identical rewrite"): a second internal tag-tracking structure, `ConcurrentDictionary<(string TenantId, string Tag), ConcurrentDictionary<(string Entity, string Id), byte>>`, populated whenever `SetAsync`'s `CachePolicy.Tags` is non-null/non-empty and consulted by `RemoveByTagAsync` to remove ONLY the calling tenant's tagged entries — proving the identical cross-tenant tag-invalidation-isolation property the real (planned) implementation exists to guarantee, not merely the narrower read/write isolation the phase's literal wording names. Deliberately an INDEPENDENT fake with its own backing store — no internal composition of `Caching/FakeCacheService`/`Caching/FakeTenantCacheKeyProvider` — continuing this folder's established "fakes share no internal state with each other" convention. `.Count` → `int` (total entries across every tenant) and `.Reset()` → `void` (clears both backing structures), mirroring `FakeCacheService`/`FakeRedisHashService`'s existing introspection/reset conventions. | T-64 | Prove the three DI registration extensions in `SharedKernel.Testing.SelfTests` — the extended `AddFakeCachingServices()` resolves `IRedisChannelService`/`IRedisHashService` as singletons alongside the pre-existing four; `AddFakeTypedHashStore<T>()` resolves `ITypedHashStore<T>` as a singleton, callable once per distinct `T` without collision; `AddFakeCacheWarmupStrategy()` registers such that multiple calls with different `name` arguments all resolve from `IEnumerable<ICacheWarmupStrategy>` (proving the multi-strategy composition mirrors `AddCacheWarmup<TStrategy>()`'s own shape). Source: P-306/WO-050, depends on C-100. **CORRECTED against C-100's own shipped code, found while proving this task**: `AddFakeCacheWarmupStrategy()` as originally shipped used `TryAddEnumerable`, which threw `ArgumentException` ("indistinguishable from other services") on the very first call — .NET's `TryAddEnumerable` infers a descriptor's "implementation type" from the factory delegate's own `Func<IServiceProvider, TService>` generic signature, not from what the factory constructs at runtime, so a `Func<IServiceProvider, ICacheWarmupStrategy>` factory is indistinguishable from the service type itself. Fixed by using the two-type-parameter `ServiceDescriptor.Singleton<TService, TImplementation>` overload — this cleared the crash but exposed a second, deeper problem: `TryAddEnumerable` de-duplicates by `(ServiceType, ImplementationType)` only, and every call constructs the same concrete `FakeCacheWarmupStrategy` type regardless of `name`/`order`/`executionLog`, so a second/third call was silently dropped rather than appended — defeating the documented "multiple independently-registered strategies" goal (unlike the real `AddCacheWarmup<TStrategy>()`, which is genuinely parameterized by a distinct generic `TStrategy` per call, so `TryAddEnumerable` correctly applies there). Fixed by switching `AddFakeCacheWarmupStrategy()` to plain `services.AddSingleton<ICacheWarmupStrategy>(factory)` (no de-duplication) — this is the actual, correct, shipped behavior as of this Tests-phase pass; `16.Testing/CLAUDE.md`'s `AddFakeCacheWarmupStrategy` Interface Contracts block and Implementation Rules bullet corrected to match (see Docs-phase/brain-sync notes). Switching to the two-type-parameter `ServiceDescriptor.Singleton<TService, TImplementation>` overload cleared the crash but exposed a second, deeper problem: `TryAddEnumerable` de-duplicates by `(ServiceType, ImplementationType)` only, and every call constructs the same concrete `FakeCacheWarmupStrategy` type regardless of `name`/`order`/`executionLog` — so a second/third differently-named call was silently dropped, never appearing in the resolved `IEnumerable<ICacheWarmupStrategy>` (defeating the documented "multiple independently-registered strategies" goal). Fixed by switching `AddFakeCacheWarmupStrategy()` to plain `services.AddSingleton<ICacheWarmupStrategy>(factory)` (no de-duplication) — unlike the real `AddCacheWarmup<TStrategy>()`, which is genuinely parameterized by a distinct generic `TStrategy` per call and for which `TryAddEnumerable` is correct, this fake extension is parameterized by a runtime string, so `TryAddEnumerable`'s per-implementation-type dedup was never actually achievable here. `16.Testing/SharedKernel.Testing/Caching/CachingServiceCollectionExtensions.cs` corrected (code + XML doc `<remarks>` explaining the deviation, per this domain's own "any `Add*` DI extension that diverges from a documented shape must carry an explanatory `<remarks>`" convention); `16.Testing/CLAUDE.md`'s `AddFakeCacheWarmupStrategy` Interface Contracts entry and its cross-reference in the DI Registration section corrected to match (see the same-day sync-brain changelog entry). `dotnet build` on both `SharedKernel.Testing.csproj`/`SharedKernel.Testing.SelfTests.csproj` succeeds 0 errors, 7/4 pre-existing warnings respectively, none introduced.
